The shared 20-point pattern

Every 7.5° hue uses these same positions. The freehand pattern bends toward the bright, saturated corner, opening room for the bottom-left sample at S = 25%, V = 25%.

Round markers are main samples; green-outlined squares are the four tinted samples, present every 30°. The background is continuous reference color, not extra palette entries. Positions show the requested coordinates before 8-bit rounding.

Loading color measurements…

16 evenly spaced OKHSV grays

S = 0, V = 0/15 through 15/15. Black and white are included. Even OKHSV value steps produce uneven sRGB byte steps.

48 tinted neutrals and deep accents

Four green points at each 30° hue mark. The darkest sample has S = 60%, V = 10%; it is a colored shadow, not a strictly low-saturation gray.

All 48 hue pages

Select any page for a larger view. Saturation increases rightward; value increases upward. All pages share the same coordinate scale.

Exact sampling coordinates and method

The top-right bias applies f(x) = x + 0.35x(1 − x) to the sketch coordinates, then snaps to 5% steps. The lowest-saturation main shadow moves to (25%, 25%) to keep all 48 hue samples distinct after byte rounding. No individual RGB colors are nudged, no samples are pruned, and no fillers are added.

The palette uses Björn Ottosson’s OKHSV reference conversion and Oklab hue angles. The directions at multiples of 30° are sampling landmarks, not conventional RGB primaries. OKHSV improves on HSV’s perceptual behavior but does not make equal coordinate steps equally visible. This geometric palette has no minimum ΔE guarantee. Numerical excursions at the reference gamut boundary are clamped before nearest-byte rounding.
